target_customer: Small and mid sized food and retail businesses such as bakeries, donut shops, cafes and ice cream shops buying custom printed packaging
problem: Small businesses faced high minimums and poor service when ordering branded packaging. Georgette made custom designed, carbon neutral packaging easy to order in small runs.
business_model: Manufacturing and sale of custom printed packaging, with carbon offsets

founders.name: Sarah Landstreet
previous_startups: A bakery in Belfast (sold after about three years)
founders.background_notes: Globe and Mail (2021-09-24). The YC page also lists mechanical engineering, an MBA and sheep shearing certification.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering and design tooling were simple; the work was in print and box manufacturing partnerships, which the founder learned by incubating at a box factory for about 18 months.

defensibility.rationale: Customers re-ordered branded packaging and the founder built supplier know how, but online custom packaging was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. The company still sold packaging in 2026 per its website.

market_need_then: The Globe and Mail (2021-09-24) reports the founder interviewed about 25 bakeries before launching and that food brands wanted packaging that stands out on social media; nearly 250 clients by 2021.

identity.visual_style: Brand pages stress Pantone matched colours and premium finishes
identity.voice_and_tone: Sustainability and ambition focused: 'packaging for ambitious businesses'

branding.community_and_virality: A Globe and Mail feature (2021-09) on the company and customer testimonials on a partner's site; no merch or community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B brand with a clear sustainability message and a feature in a national paper, but no evidence of broad recognition.

outcome_analysis: Georgette Packaging grew from a solo founder in 2013 to 14 staff and nearly 250 clients by 2021, with a sustainability positioning and only a small YC investment recorded. YC marks it inactive but the website still sells packaging and directories show it alive, so the status conflict is unresolved and no failure is asserted.
notes: YC status is Inactive but the website was live and other directories (Velocity Incubator, CB Insights) list it active, so the status conflict is recorded here. The $120K seed rests on aggregators (CB Insights dates it 2016-03-15, Persana says pre-seed 2016-04-22). Other directories name different leaders (Jennifer Appleby Vines, Mansur Kanchwala); not listed as founders without an opened source. Competitor search found Packlane (founded 2015 per its about page, undated) and noissue (2017, too late); neither has a source dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Name origin not sourced.
